title: Keyboard Manager: remapping Right Alt + . to Play/Pause causes Ctrl to get stuck

fix_assessment.rationale: The reported Right Alt shortcut enters Keyboard Manager's explicit AltGr modifier-state path, making leaked synthetic Ctrl state a plausible but unconfirmed cause. The exact keyboard layout, trigger sequence and post-reproduction diagnostics are missing, so the proposal remains low-confidence and requests discriminating evidence before a detailed design.

proposed_fixes.title: Guard AltGr modifier cleanup for media-key remaps
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The AltGr state-tracking path may mishandle the key-up sequence when Right Alt plus a character is remapped to a media key, leaving the synthetic left Ctrl state active after the shortcut finishes.
plan: Add an engine regression test for the reported Right Alt plus period to Play/Pause mapping, modeling the synthetic left-Ctrl event that Windows may send for AltGr and asserting that both Ctrl and the media key are released after the full sequence.

Trace the `isAltRightKeyInvoked` state through `KeyboardEventHandlers` and the modifier restoration helpers; change release ordering or state ownership only if the regression demonstrates a leak, while preserving physically held Ctrl and AltGr state.
Add adjacent coverage for the reported key-up ordering and for a non-AltGr Right Alt layout.
verification: Run the focused Keyboard Manager engine shortcut-remapping tests, including the new media-key/AltGr regression.
On the reporter's keyboard layout, repeat the mapping and trigger sequence and confirm Ctrl is not held after the remapped action completes.

confidence.rationale: Current source has dedicated AltGr state handling, but the report lacks the active keyboard layout, exact trigger/release sequence and a diagnostic capture; no failing path is yet confirmed.

issue_context.summary: A Right Alt plus period shortcut mapped to Play/Pause can leave Ctrl apparently held in Keyboard Manager on v0.102.3001.
known_information: The report specifies PowerToys v0.102.3001 and a Right Alt + period to Play/Pause remap.
The user reports that left Ctrl becomes stuck intermittently and that pressing Ctrl clears it temporarily.
The current live labels identify Keyboard Manager; the body is unchanged and there are no follow-up comments.
Current upstream KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp tracks the synthetic Ctrl component of AltGr and has distinct cleanup logic for shortcut-to-key remaps.
Existing OSLevelShortcutRemappingTests.cpp exercises AltGr followed by an LCtrl+Y to Backspace remap, but not the reported Right Alt + period to media-key sequence.
inferences: If the active layout treats Right Alt as AltGr, Windows may send a synthetic left-Ctrl event; a key-up ordering issue in the remapped action path could account for the symptom.
The report does not yet establish that AltGr is active or that the AltGr cleanup path is the cause.
issue_context.analysis: The current code already contains explicit AltGr bookkeeping, so a generic modifier-release fix would be unsafe. The key distinction is whether the reporter's Right Alt is AltGr and which release sequence leaves Ctrl down. Request those details and a fresh bug report, then reproduce the exact media-key mapping before changing state cleanup.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue report and searched current open and historical Keyboard Manager reports; issue 9778 is a broader older stuck-modifier report, not proof of the same mapping or cause.
Inspected current upstream `src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEngineLibrary/KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp` at the Right-Alt/AltGr detection and shortcut-to-key cleanup paths.
Inspected `src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEngineTest/OSLevelShortcutRemappingTests.cpp`; existing AltGr tests do not cover the reported media-key mapping.
No exact reproduction, environment-specific confirmation or diagnostic evidence is available, so the proposed root cause remains a hypothesis.

information_gaps.information: The active Windows keyboard layout and whether Right Alt acts as AltGr
information_gaps.why_needed: Windows may synthesize left Ctrl for AltGr, which determines whether the dedicated AltGr state path is involved.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Report the active keyboard layout/input language shown in Windows Settings and confirm whether Right Alt is AltGr.

information_gaps.information: The exact key press/release sequence, app and repeatability of the stuck-Ctrl behavior
information_gaps.why_needed: The current report names the remapping but does not identify which trigger or key-up sequence leaves Ctrl active.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: List the physical keys pressed and released in order, the foreground app, and whether the issue occurs on every attempt or intermittently.

information_gaps.information: A fresh PowerToys bug report captured immediately after Ctrl becomes stuck
information_gaps.why_needed: The trace can show whether the remapped action and synthetic AltGr modifier were released before the state was manually cleared.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: If it happens again, add `/bugreport` immediately after Ctrl sticks and before pressing Ctrl to reset it.

judgment.rationale: A specific AltGr modifier-state cleanup path is plausible and can be tested with a narrow regression, but the root cause is not confirmed. The red-confidence proposal is paired with an exact request for the layout, sequence and diagnostic evidence needed to validate or reject it.
judgment.recommended_action: Request the active keyboard layout, exact trigger/release sequence and a fresh /bugreport after reproduction; use those details to confirm or reject the AltGr cleanup hypothesis before implementation.
evidence: The issue identifies v0.102.3001, Right Alt + period mapped to Play/Pause, and a temporarily stuck Ctrl state.
Current upstream `KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp` sets `isAltRightKeyInvoked` when Right Alt follows left Ctrl and has separate modifier restoration logic for remapped keys.
The existing AltGr regression tests do not cover the reported Right Alt plus period to media-key mapping.
Historical issue 9778 describes broad stuck-modifier symptoms but does not establish this specific trigger or a covering fix.
The latest live update added the Product-Keyboard Manager label; the issue body and zero-comment discussion are unchanged.

comment.body:
Thanks for narrowing this to Right Alt + `.` mapped to Play/Pause on v0.102.3001, and for noting that pressing Ctrl temporarily clears the stuck state. Keyboard Manager has a special path for Right Alt acting as AltGr, so the missing layout and key-up sequence determine whether that path is involved. Could you share:

- The Windows version/build and active keyboard layout, and whether Right Alt acts as AltGr.
- The exact physical key press/release sequence and foreground app, plus whether Ctrl gets stuck on every attempt or intermittently.
- If it happens again, a `/bugreport` captured immediately after Ctrl sticks and before pressing Ctrl to clear it.

This will let us reproduce the media-key mapping without guessing at the modifier state.
